scope: Descriptions of seven historical rule specimens; no outline changes.

entries.name: Brass rule No. 1, thin and thick sections
entries.observed: A narrow line occupies the left half; a separate wider rectangular section occupies the right half. The wider section increases across Nos.1–6.
entries.interpretation: Probable printing-face and body-width comparison. This is an interpretation of the unlabeled sections, supported by the explicitly labeled FACE and BODY columns in the GPO1904 specimen, printed page16. It is not a claim that the Baltimore page itself labels these sections.
entries.artwork: Existing complete historical specimen retained; identity, codepoint, outlines and spacing unchanged.

entries.name: Two fine parallel rules
entries.observed: Two fine continuous parallel rules, with approximately equal stroke weight and a wider central interval.
entries.interpretation: Two fine continuous parallel lines with compatible line-width-to-centre-spacing proportions in three native sections. Differences in stock length, source resolution and ink spread do not establish a new design. This is a design correspondence, not evidence of shared physical matrices or an inferred Baltimore point size.
entries.artwork: Existing identity, codepoint, outlines and spacing unchanged. Baltimore remains the preferred drawing source.
